name: read-file-lazy
doc: Returns a lazy sequence of byte chunks from a file.

name: read-string
doc: Reads the first phel expression from the string s.

name: realized?
doc: Returns true if a lazy sequence, delay, promise, or future has been realized, false otherwise.

name: rebuild-hierarchy
doc: Rebuilds :ancestors and :descendants maps from the :parents map in h.

name: reduce
doc:
Reduces collection to a single value by repeatedly applying function to accumulator and elements.
  Respects early termination via `(reduced val)`.

name: reduced
doc: Wraps `x` in a Reduced, signaling early termination from reduce/transduce.

name: reduced?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a Reduced value.

name: register-protocol-implementor!
doc:
Records that `type-key` implements the protocol identified by both
  `protocol-value` (the `defprotocol` map) and `protocol-tag` (its FQN
  string). Called from `extend-type`'s expansion.

name: reify
doc:
Creates an anonymous object implementing one or more protocols.
  Method bodies close over local bindings. Each instance carries its
  own captured state, so reify works correctly inside loops.

  Syntax:
    (reify
      ProtocolName
      (method-name [this arg1] body)
      AnotherProtocol
      (another-method [this] body))

name: rem
doc:
Returns the truncated remainder of `dividend` / `divisor`. The result
  has the same sign as `dividend` (matches PHP's `%`).

name: remove
doc:
Returns a lazy sequence of elements where predicate returns false.
   Opposite of filter. When called with pred only, returns a transducer.

name: remove-ns
doc:
Removes the namespace and all of its definitions from the registry.
  Use with caution. Returns nil.

name: remove-tap
doc: Removes `f` from the tap set. Returns nil.

name: remove-watch
doc: Removes a watch function from a variable by key.

name: rename-keys
doc:
Returns the map with keys renamed according to kmap.
  Keys not present in kmap are left unchanged.

name: repeat
doc:
Returns a vector of length n where every element is x.

  With one argument returns an infinite lazy sequence of x.

name: repeatedly
doc:
Returns a vector of length n with values produced by repeatedly calling f.

  With one argument returns an infinite lazy sequence of calls to f.

name: reset-meta!
doc:
Installs `meta-map` as the metadata on `r`, replacing any prior metadata.
  Works on `Var` handles and on atoms. Returns the installed map.

name: reset!
doc: Sets a new value on the given atom. Returns the new value.

name: resolve
doc: Resolves the given symbol in the current environment and returns a resolved Symbol with the absolute namespace or nil if it cannot be resolved.

name: rest
doc: Returns the sequence after the first element, or empty sequence if none.

name: reverse
doc: Reverses the order of the elements in the given sequence.

name: reversible?
doc:
Returns true if `coll` can be reverse-iterated in constant time.
  Currently this is true for vectors, sorted-maps, and sorted-sets.

name: round
doc:
Rounds `x` to the nearest integer using PHP's `round` (half away from
  zero). Ints and `BigInt` values are returned unchanged. Ratios
  and floats return floats.

name: rseq
doc:
Returns, in constant time, a sequence of the items in `rev` in reverse
  order. `rev` must be reversible (a vector, sorted-map, or sorted-set);
  otherwise an exception is thrown. For sorted-maps, returns reversed `[key value]` pairs.
  Returns nil if `rev` is empty.

name: run!
doc: Calls `(f x)` for each element in `coll` for side effects. Returns nil.

name: satisfies?
doc: Returns true if x's type implements all methods of the given protocol.

name: second
doc: Returns the second element of a sequence, or nil if not present.

name: select-keys
doc: Returns a new map including key value pairs from `m` selected with keys `ks`.

name: seq
doc:
Returns a seq on the collection. Strings are converted to a vector of characters.
  Other non-empty collections (vectors, sets, sorted-maps, sorted-sets, PHP arrays)
  are converted to a non-list seq. Returns nil if `coll` is empty or nil.

  This function is useful for explicitly converting strings to sequences of characters,
  enabling sequence operations like map, filter, and frequencies.

name: seq?
doc:
Returns true if `x` is a seq (a list, a lazy sequence, or a realized
  `Cons` cell returned by `(next some-lazy-seq)`).

name: seqable?
doc:
Returns true if `(seq x)` is supported: collections (vectors, lists,
   maps, sets, structs), lazy sequences, strings, PHP arrays, and nil.
   Returns false for numbers, booleans, keywords, symbols, and other types.

name: sequence
doc: Applies transducer `xform` to `coll`, returning a vector of results.

name: sequential?
doc:
Returns true if `x` is a sequential collection (vector, list, or lazy
   sequence), false otherwise. Sequential collections maintain insertion
   order and support indexed or linear access. Maps, sets, and structs
   are not sequential, matching Clojure's `Sequential` marker.

name: set
doc:
Coerces a collection to a set. Returns a set containing the distinct elements of `coll`.
  For creating sets from arguments, use `hash-set`.

name: set-validator!
doc:
Sets a validator function on a variable. The validator is called before any
  state change with the proposed new value. If it returns a falsy value, an
  exception is thrown and the state is not changed. Pass nil to remove.

name: set?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a set, false otherwise.

name: short
doc:
Coerces `x` to a signed 16-bit integer in the range `-32768..32767`.
   Decimal values are truncated toward zero. `Ratio` and `BigInt`
   values are accepted (truncate toward zero, then range-check). Values
   outside the range or non-numeric inputs raise `InvalidArgumentException`.
   Phel has no dedicated short type, so the result is a plain PHP int.

name: short-array
doc:
Creates a PHP array of shorts (16-bit integers). Accepts the same arities
  and semantics as `int-array`.

name: shuffle
doc: Returns a random permutation of coll.

name: simple-ident?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a symbol or keyword without a namespace.

name: simple-keyword?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a keyword without a namespace.

name: simple-symbol?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a symbol without a namespace.

name: slice
doc: Extracts a slice of `coll` starting at `offset` with optional `length`.

name: slurp
doc: Reads entire file or URL into a string.

name: some
doc: Returns the first truthy value of applying predicate to elements, or nil if none found.

name: some->
doc: Threads `x` through the forms like `->` but stops when a form returns `nil`.

name: some->>
doc: Threads `x` through the forms like `->>` but stops when a form returns `nil`.

name: some-fn
doc:
Takes a variadic set of predicates and returns a function `f` that,
   when called with any number of arguments, returns the first logical
   true value produced by applying any of the composing predicates to
   any of its arguments, and `false` when none match. The returned
   function short-circuits on the first truthy result: arguments after
   it are not inspected, and predicates after it are not tried.
   Predicates are consulted in the order supplied; for a given
   predicate, arguments are consulted left-to-right.
example:
((some-fn even? nil?) 1 2) ; => true
((some-fn pos? even?) -3 -1) ; => false

name: some?
doc:
With 1 arg, returns true if `x` is not nil (Clojure semantics).
   With 2 args, returns true if `pred` is true for at least one element in `coll`.

name: sort
doc: Returns a sorted vector. If no comparator is supplied compare is used.

name: sort-by
doc:
Returns a sorted vector where the sort order is determined by comparing `(keyfn item)`.

  If no comparator is supplied compare is used.

name: sort-comparator
doc:
Wraps the user-supplied comparator (or `compare` when absent) so its
  result is always an integer. A predicate-style comparator that
  returns a boolean follows Clojure semantics: a truthy result means
  the first argument should sort earlier (`-1`), the reverse-truthy
  case means it should sort later (`+1`), otherwise the items are
  considered equal.

name: sorted-map
doc:
Creates a new sorted map. Keys are in natural sorted order.
  The number of parameters must be even.

name: sorted-map-by
doc:
Creates a new sorted map using the given comparator for key ordering.
  The comparator takes two arguments and returns a negative integer,
  zero, or a positive integer.
example: (sorted-map-by (fn [a b] (compare b a)) :a 1 :b 2) ; keys iterate as :b :a

name: sorted-set
doc: Creates a new sorted set. Elements are in natural sorted order.

name: sorted-set-by
doc: Creates a new sorted set using the given comparator for element ordering.

name: sorted?
doc: Returns true if `coll` is a sorted collection (sorted-map or sorted-set), false otherwise.

name: special-symbol?
doc: Returns true if `s` names a special form.

name: special-symbols
doc:
The set of symbols that name Phel special forms, including the
  syntactic markers `&`, `catch`, and `finally` recognised by `fn`,
  `let`, and `try`.

name: spit
doc:
Writes data to file, returning number of bytest that were written or `nil`
  on failure. Accepts `opts` map for overriding default PHP file_put_contents
  arguments, as example to append to file use `{:flags php/FILE_APPEND}`.

  See PHP's [file_put_contents](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.file-put-contents.php) for more information.

name: split-at
doc: Returns a vector of `[(take n coll) (drop n coll)]`.

name: split-with
doc: Returns a vector of `[(take-while pred coll) (drop-while pred coll)]`.

name: sqrt
doc:
Returns the square root of `x` as a float. Negative inputs return
  `##NaN` (matches PHP's `sqrt`).

name: str
doc:
Creates a string by concatenating values together. If no arguments are
provided an empty string is returned. Nil is represented as an empty string.
Booleans are represented as "true" or "false" (matching Clojure semantics).
Otherwise, it tries to call `__toString`.

name: str-contains?
doc: Returns true if str contains s.

name: string?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a string, false otherwise.

name: struct?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a struct, false otherwise.

name: subset?
doc: Returns true if `s1` is a subset of `s2`, i.e. every element in `s1` is also in `s2`.

name: sum
doc: Returns the sum of all elements is `xs`.

name: superset?
doc: Returns true if `s1` is a superset of `s2`, i.e. every element in `s2` is also in `s1`.

name: swap!
doc:
Atomically swaps the value of the atom to `(apply f current-value args)`.

  Returns the new value after the swap.

name: symbol
doc:
Returns a new symbol for the given name with an optional namespace.

  With one argument, creates a symbol without namespace. Accepts a
  string, a keyword, another symbol, or a `Var` (in which case the
  result is a fully qualified symbol naming the var). With two
  arguments, creates a symbol in the given namespace; a `nil`
  namespace yields a symbol without a namespace.

  Throws `InvalidArgumentException` for any other input (including
  functions, numbers, and collections).

name: symbol?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a symbol, false otherwise.

name: symmetric-difference
doc: Symmetric difference between multiple sets into a new one.

name: take
doc:
Takes the first `n` elements of `coll`.
  When called with n only, returns a transducer.

name: take-last
doc: Takes the last `n` elements of `coll`.

name: take-nth
doc:
Returns every nth item in `coll`. Returns a lazy sequence.
  When called with n only, returns a transducer.

name: take-while
doc:
Takes all elements at the front of `coll` where `(pred x)` is true. Returns a lazy sequence.
  When called with pred only, returns a transducer.

name: tap>
doc:
Sends `x` to every registered tap. Exceptions thrown by individual taps are
  swallowed so one misbehaving tap does not affect the others. Returns true.

name: thread-bound?
doc:
Returns true when a fiber-local `binding` (or `with-bindings`) frame
  currently overrides the value of `v` on the calling fiber.

name: time
doc: Evaluates expr and prints the time it took. Returns the value of expr.

name: to-array
doc:
Returns a PHP array containing the elements of `coll`. Accepts any
  collection (vector, list, set, map, PHP array) or `nil`, which yields
  an empty PHP array. Matches Clojure's `to-array` for `.cljc` interop —
  in Phel the result is a plain PHP array since PHP has no `Object[]`.
example:
(to-array [1 2 3]) ; => a PHP array [1, 2, 3]
(to-array nil) ; => a PHP array []

name: to-symbol-part
doc:
Extracts the underlying string from `x` for use as a symbol or
  namespace component. Keywords and symbols pass through their `name`.

name: transduce
doc:
Reduce with a transformation of `f` (xf). If init is not supplied,
  `(f)` will be called to produce it. `f` should be a reducing function
  that returns the initial value when called with no arguments.

name: transient
doc:
Converts a persistent collection to a transient collection for efficient updates.

  Transient collections provide faster performance for multiple sequential updates.
  Use `persistent` to convert back.

name: tree-seq
doc:
Returns a vector of the nodes in the tree, via a depth-first walk.
  branch? is a function with one argument that returns true if the given node
  has children.
  children must be a function with one argument that returns the children of the node.
  root the root node of the tree.

name: true?
doc: Checks if value is exactly true (not just truthy).

name: truthy?
doc: Checks if `x` is truthy. Same as `x == true` in PHP.

name: type
doc:
Returns the type of `x`. The following types can be returned:

* `:vector`
* `:list`
* `:struct`
* `:hash-map`
* `:map-entry`
* `:set`
* `:keyword`
* `:symbol`
* `:atom`
* `:var`
* `:int`
* `:float`
* `:ratio`
* `:bigint`
* `:bigdec`
* `:uuid`
* `:php/class`
* `:queue`
* `:string`
* `:nil`
* `:boolean`
* `:function`
* `:php/array`
* `:php/resource`
* `:php/object`
* `:unknown`

name: underive
doc:
Removes a parent/child relationship.
  With two arguments, mutates the global hierarchy and returns nil.
  With a hierarchy `h`, returns a new hierarchy without the relationship;
  the original is unchanged.

name: union
doc: Union multiple sets into a new one.

name: unreduced
doc: If `x` is Reduced, returns the unwrapped value; otherwise returns `x`.

name: unset
doc: Returns `ds` without `key`.

name: unset-in
doc: Removes a value from a nested data structure.

name: unwrap-future
doc:
Returns the raw Amp\Future for either a `Future` wrapper or
  a bare `Amp\Future`.

name: update
doc: Updates a value in a datastructure by applying `f` to the current value.

name: update-in
doc: Updates a value in a nested data structure by applying `f` to the value at path.

name: update-keys
doc: Returns a map with `f` applied to each key.

name: update-vals
doc: Returns a map with `f` applied to each value.

name: uuid-nil?
doc: Returns true if `x` is the nil UUID (all zeros), false otherwise.

name: uuid-variant
doc:
Returns a keyword describing the variant field of UUID `x`: `:ncs`,
  `:rfc-4122`, `:microsoft`, or `:reserved`. Returns nil if `x` is not a
  `UUID` value.

name: uuid-version
doc:
Returns the version digit (1-5) encoded in UUID `x`, or nil if `x` is
  not a `UUID` value.

name: uuid?
doc:
Returns true if `x` is a `Phel\Lang\UUID` value, false otherwise.
  Canonical UUID strings are rejected — wrap them with `parse-uuid` (or
  the `#uuid "..."` literal) to obtain a typed value.

name: uuid=
doc:
Returns true if `a` and `b` are `Phel\Lang\UUID` values with the
  same canonical form. Strings (or anything else) are rejected even if
  their textual content would match — coerce with `parse-uuid` first.

name: val
doc:
Returns the value of a map entry. Accepts a typed
  `Phel\Lang\Collections\Map\MapEntry` value or a 2-element vector
  `[key value]`.

name: val-to-str
doc:
Converts a value to its string representation. Booleans become "true" or
"false". Nil becomes an empty string. Integer-valued floats keep their `.0`
suffix (so `(str 0.0)` is `"0.0"`, not `"0"`). All other values use PHP
string cast.

name: valid-hierarchy-parents
doc: Returns h's parents map when h has the expected hierarchy shape.

name: vals
doc:
Returns a sequence of all values in a map, or `nil` when the map is `nil`
  or empty.

name: values
doc: Returns a sequence of all values in a map.

name: var-get
doc:
Resolves the value bound to a `Var` or to a fully-qualified symbol.

  Accepts a `Var` instance (typically from `(var sym)` or `#'sym`) and
  returns its current root value. Accepts a fully-qualified symbol and
  reads the matching definition from the registry; tries the symbol name
  verbatim first, then the encoded form, so it pairs with both `def` and
  `intern`.

  With one argument, returns nil when the symbol is not defined. With two
  arguments, returns `not-found` instead, which lets callers disambiguate a
  stored nil from a missing definition. Returns `not-found` for non-symbol
  or unqualified inputs.

name: var-set
doc:
Sets the value of the topmost active fiber-local binding frame for
  `v` to `val`. Throws when no `binding` (or `with-bindings`) frame is
  currently overriding `v`. Returns `val`.

name: var?
doc:
Returns true if the given value is a `Var`, the first-class handle to a
  global definition produced by `(var sym)` and `#'sym`.

name: vec
doc:
Coerces a collection to a vector. For hash-maps and structs, entries
  are returned as 2-element `[key value]` vectors, matching Clojure.

name: vector?
doc:
Returns true if `x` is a vector. Map entries returned by iterating a
  hash map (`(first {:a 1})`) are vector-shaped two-element values, so
  this predicate also accepts the typed `MapEntry`.

name: volatile!
doc:
Creates a volatile mutable reference with initial value `val`.
  Use for transducer state that needs fast mutation without watches.

name: volatile?
doc: Returns true if `x` is a Volatile.

name: vreset!
doc: Sets the value of volatile `vol` to `val`. Returns `val`.

name: vswap!
doc:
Applies `f` to the current value of volatile `vol` plus `args`,
  and sets the new value. Returns the new value.

name: when
doc: Evaluates body if test is true, otherwise returns nil.

name: when-first
doc:
Binds name to the first element of coll. When the collection is non-empty
  (first returns non-nil), evaluates body with the binding.

name: when-let
doc: When test is true, evaluates body with binding-form bound to the value of test

name: when-not
doc: Evaluates body if test is false, otherwise returns nil.

name: when-some
doc:
Binds name to the value of test. When test is not nil, evaluates body with
  binding-form bound to the value of test. Unlike when-let, false and 0 are not
  treated as falsy — only nil causes the body to be skipped.

name: with-bindings
doc:
Like `binding` but takes a map of `Var -> value` instead of a binding
  vector. Same dynamic-only enforcement: throws when any key resolves
  to a non-dynamic var.

name: with-output-buffer
doc:
Everything that is printed inside the body will be stored in a buffer.
   The result of the buffer is returned.

name: with-redefs
doc:
Temporarily replaces the root values of vars while executing `body`.

  Accepts any var, dynamic or not. The previous root values are
  captured before `body` runs and restored on exit, including when
  `body` throws. The replacement is process-global: every fiber sees
  the new root for the duration of the body, which makes this a
  convenient mocking primitive for tests but unsafe for concurrent
  production code. Use `binding` for fiber-local rebinding of
  `^:dynamic` vars.

name: xf-step
doc:
Creates a transducer reducing function that delegates 0/1 arity to rf
  and calls step-fn for the 2-arity step. Eliminates repeated boilerplate.

name: zero?
doc: Checks if `x` is zero.

name: zipcoll
doc: Creates a map from two sequential data structures. Returns a new map.

name: zipmap
doc:
Returns a new map with the keys mapped to the corresponding values.

  Stops when the shorter of `keys` or `vals` is exhausted.
  Works safely with infinite lazy sequences.

name: install-readers
doc: Registers each `tag -> fn` from `readers` on the registry.

name: read-next
doc:
Reads the next form from the open `token-stream` using `cf`. Skips
  whitespace, comments, and other trivia parser nodes that precede the
  next data form. Returns nil when the stream is exhausted.

name: read-string
doc:
Reads one EDN value from string `s`.

  When `s` is empty or only whitespace/comments, returns the `:eof` value
  from `opts` (default nil).

  Options:
    :readers  map of tag (symbol, keyword, or string) to 1-arg handler fn
    :eof      value returned for empty input

name: read-string-all
doc:
Reads every EDN value from string `s` and returns them as a vector.

  Options:
    :readers  map of tag (symbol, keyword, or string) to 1-arg handler fn

name: restore-tags
doc:
Reinstates the original handlers captured by `snapshot-tags`. When a
  tag had no prior handler, it is unregistered so the registry returns to
  its earlier shape.

name: snapshot-tags
doc:
Captures the existing handler for each tag key so it can be restored
  after the call. Returns a map `{tag-key handler-or-nil}`.

name: tag-key
doc:
Normalises a tag from a symbol, keyword, or string to the string key
  used by the global `TagRegistry`.

name: with-readers*
doc:
Runs `thunk` with `readers` temporarily installed on the tag registry.
  Restores prior state in a `finally` so exceptions still clean up.

name: write-string
doc:
Serialises `value` to its EDN string representation. Uses Phel's
  readable printer so the output round-trips through `read-string` for
  all EDN-compatible values (nil, booleans, numbers, strings, keywords,
  symbols, lists, vectors, maps, sets, and built-in tagged literals
  such as `#uuid`).

name: write-string-all
doc:
Serialises a sequence of values to EDN, separating top-level forms
  with a single space. Inverse of `read-string-all`.

name: compile-element
doc: Compiles a element.

name: doctype
doc: Returns an HTML doctype declaration.

name: escape-html
doc: Escapes HTML special characters to prevent XSS.

name: html
doc: Compiles Phel vectors to HTML strings.

name: render-element
doc: Renders an Element.

name: unevaluated?
doc: An expression is unevaluated if it is a symbol or it is not quoted.

name: append-query-params
doc: Appends query parameters to a URL string.

name: build-headers-array
doc: Converts a Phel header map to a PHP associative array.

name: build-options-array
doc: Converts Phel options to a PHP associative array for the transport.

name: delete
doc: Makes a DELETE request. See `request` for available options.

name: get
doc: Makes a GET request. See `request` for available options.

name: head
doc: Makes a HEAD request. See `request` for available options.

name: key->string
doc: Converts a keyword or string key to its string form.

name: patch
doc: Makes a PATCH request. See `request` for available options.

name: post
doc: Makes a POST request. See `request` for available options.

name: put
doc: Makes a PUT request. See `request` for available options.

name: request
doc:
Makes an HTTP request and returns an http/response struct.

  `method` is a keyword or string (:get, :post, "PUT", etc.).
  `url` is the target URL string.
  `opts` is an optional map with:
    :headers          - Map of header name to value
    :body             - String request body
    :json             - Value to JSON-encode as body (sets Content-Type)
    :query-params     - Map of query parameters to append to URL
    :timeout          - Timeout in seconds as float (default 30.0)
    :follow-redirects - Follow HTTP redirects (default true)
    :verify-ssl       - Verify SSL certificates (default true)
signature: (request method url & [{:headers headers :body body :json json-body :query-params query-params :timeout timeout :follow-redirects follow-redirects :verify-ssl verify-ssl}])

name: transport-result->response
doc: Converts a transport result PHP array to an http/response struct.

name: emit-response
doc: Emits the response by sending headers and outputting the body.

name: encode-utf-8-url
doc: Prepares utf-8 urls from php/parse-url.

name: files-from-globals
doc: Extracts the files from `$_FILES` and normalizes them to a map of "uploaded-file".

name: get-method-from-globals
doc: Extracts the request method from `$_SERVER`.

name: headers-from-server
doc: Extracts all headers from the `$_SERVER` variable.

name: host-and-port-from-globals
doc: Extract the host and port from the `$_SERVER` array.

name: request-from-globals
doc: Extracts a request from `$_SERVER`, `$_GET`, `$_POST`, `$_COOKIE` and `$_FILES`.

name: request-from-globals-args
doc: Extracts a request from args.
example: (request-from-globals-args php/$_SERVER php/$_GET php/$_POST php/$_COOKIE php/$_FILES) ; => (request "GET" (uri ...) {...} nil {...} {...} {...} {...} "1.1" {})

name: request-from-map
doc: Creates a request struct from a map with optional keys :method, :uri, :headers, etc.
signature: (request-from-map {:method method :uri uri :headers headers :parsed-body parsed-body :query-params query-params :cookie-params cookie-params :server-params server-params :uploaded-files uploaded-files :version version :attributes attributes})

name: response-from-map
doc: Creates a response struct from a map with optional keys :status, :headers, :body, :version, and :reason.

name: response-from-string
doc: Create a response from a string.

name: uri-from-globals
doc: Extracts the URI from the `$_SERVER` variable.

name: uri-from-string
doc: Create a uri struct from a string.

name: decode
doc: Decodes a JSON string to a Phel value.

name: decode-value
doc: Converts a JSON value to Phel format.

name: encode
doc: Encodes a Phel value to a JSON string.

name: encode-value
doc: Converts a Phel value to JSON-compatible format.

name: valid-key?
doc: Checks if a value can be used as a JSON key.

name: and-checks
doc:
Combines a seq of boolean checks into a single expression, skipping
  `true` and collapsing a single check.

name: binding-symbol?
doc: A bare symbol that is neither the wildcard nor the rest marker.

name: compile-as
doc: (inner :as name): bind target to name, recurse on inner.

name: compile-clause
doc: Compiles one clause row into `[check bindings]`.

name: compile-guard
doc:
(inner :guard pred): compile inner, and-combine with (pred target)
  evaluated in the context of the inner bindings so the guard can see
  bound symbols.

name: compile-map
doc: Map pattern: shape check, key-presence check, recurse on each value.

name: compile-or
doc:
(:or p1 p2 ...): succeeds if any alternative matches. Alternatives
  may not introduce bindings (keeps v1 simple and predictable).

name: compile-pattern
doc:
Dispatches on pattern shape and delegates to the kind-specific
  compiler. Returns `{:check expr :bindings [sym val ...]}`.

name: compile-vector
doc:
Vector pattern: shape + length check, recursively compile each
  element, optionally bind the rest of the slice.

name: index-of-rest
doc:
Linear scan for `&` inside a vector, comparing with `=` so that
  freshly-read symbols match the `'&` literal. Returns the index or
  nil.

name: match
doc:
Matches a vector of targets against pattern/expression clauses and
  returns the first matching expression.

  Supported patterns:
  - literal values (numbers, strings, keywords, booleans, nil)
  - `_` wildcard
  - bare symbol: binds the value to that name in the clause body
  - vector pattern `[a b c]`, with optional rest `[a & tail]`
  - map pattern `{:k1 p1 :k2 p2}` — keys must be present in the target
  - `(inner :guard pred)` — matches if `(pred bound)` is truthy
  - `(inner :as name)` — binds the whole value to `name`
  - `(:or p1 p2 ...)` — matches any alternative (no inner bindings)

  A trailing `:else expr` provides the default branch; without it a
  no-match raises `\RuntimeException`.

name: parse-clauses
doc:
Walks the body splitting it into `[clauses default]`. `clauses` is a
  vector of `[pattern-vec expr]`, `default` is the `:else` expression
  or `nil`.

name: scalar-literal?
doc: Primitives we should match by equality.

name: sequential-shape-check
doc: Runtime predicate accepting vectors, lists, and PHP arrays.

name: shape-gated-check
doc:
Wraps an inner and-combined check behind a shape predicate. When the
  target fails the shape check the expression short-circuits to `false`
  so the inner accessors never see a mismatched value.

name: split-vector-pattern
doc:
Splits a vector pattern around `&`. Returns `[head tail-sym-or-nil]`.
  Errors if `&` is not followed by exactly one symbol.

name: call-count
doc: Returns the number of times the mock was called.

name: called-once?
doc: Returns true if the mock was called exactly once.

name: called-times?
doc: Returns true if the mock was called exactly n times.

name: called-with?
doc: Returns true if the mock was called with the exact arguments.

name: called?
doc: Returns true if the mock was called at least once.

name: calls
doc: Returns a list of all argument lists the mock was called with.

name: clear-all-mocks!
doc:
Clears the entire mock registry.
  Useful for cleanup between test suites in long-running processes.

name: first-call
doc: Returns the arguments from the first call.

name: last-call
doc: Returns the arguments from the most recent call.

name: mock
doc: Creates a mock function that returns a fixed value and tracks all calls.

name: mock-fn
doc: Creates a mock function with custom behavior that tracks all calls.

name: mock-returning
doc:
Creates a mock that returns different values for consecutive calls.
  After exhausting values, returns the last value.

name: mock-throwing
doc: Creates a mock that throws an exception when called.

name: mock?
doc: Returns true if the function is a mock.

name: never-called?
doc: Returns true if the mock was never called.

name: register-mock!
doc: Registers a mock function with its call history and optional reset function

name: reset-mock!
doc:
Resets the call history of a mock without removing it from the registry.
  The mock can continue to be used and track new calls.

name: spy
doc: Wraps an existing function to track calls while preserving original behavior.

name: with-mock-wrapper
doc:
Like with-mocks but for wrapped mocks (interop scenarios).
  Automatically resets the underlying mock even when wrapped in an adapter function.

  Usage:
    ```phel
    (with-mock-wrapper [fn-symbol underlying-mock wrapper-fn]
      body...)
    ```

  Multiple wrappers:
    ```phel
    (with-mock-wrapper [service-a mock-a (fn [x] (mock-a (inc x)))
                        service-b mock-b (fn [y] (mock-b (dec y)))]
      ...)
    ```

name: with-mocks
doc:
Temporarily replaces functions with mocks using `with-redefs`.
  Automatically resets mocks after the body executes.

  Works with inline mock creation:
    ```phel
    (with-mocks [http-get (mock {:status 200})]
      (http-get)
      ;; Mock is automatically reset after this block)
    ```

  Also works with pre-defined mocks:
    ```phel
    (let [my-mock (mock :result)]
      (with-mocks [some-fn my-mock]
        (some-fn)))
    ```

  If you need to wrap the mock in a function (e.g., to adapt arguments),
  you'll need to manually reset:
    ```phel
    (with-mocks [some-fn (fn [& args] (my-mock (transform args)))]
      (some-fn)
      (reset-mock! my-mock))
    ```

name: pp-str
doc: Pretty-prints `form` to a string with the given indent level and max width.

name: pprint
doc: Pretty-prints `form` to stdout with optional `width` (default 72).

name: pprint-str
doc: Pretty-prints `form` to a string with optional `width` (default 72).

name: print-value
doc: Prints a scalar or non-collection value using the standard readable printer.

name: register-tag
doc:
Registers a handler for reader tag `tag-name` (a string without the
  leading `#`). The handler `f` is a 1-arg function receiving the
  already-read form value and returning the value that should replace
  the tagged literal.

  Re-registering an existing tag overwrites the previous handler.

name: registered-tags
doc:
Returns a sorted vector of the currently registered reader tag
  names.

name: registry
doc: Returns the shared TagRegistry singleton.

name: tag-registered?
doc: Returns true if a handler is registered for reader tag `tag-name`.

name: unregister-tag
doc:
Removes any handler registered for reader tag `tag-name`. Built-in
  tags can be unregistered but are re-installed on the next reader
  bootstrap.

name: class-info
doc:
Returns a map describing `class-or-name` with `:name`, `:methods`,
  `:properties`, `:parents`, and `:interfaces` keys.

name: methods
doc:
Returns a vector of method maps for `class-or-name`. Each map contains
  `:name`, `:params`, `:return-type`, `:static?`, and `:visibility`.

name: properties
doc:
Returns a vector of property maps for `class-or-name`. Each map contains
  `:name`, `:type`, `:static?`, `:readonly?`, and `:visibility`.

name: reflection-class
doc: Returns a ReflectionClass for `class-or-name` (string FQN or object).

name: supers
doc:
Returns a set of fully qualified parent classes and implemented
  interfaces for `class-or-name`.

name: type-string
doc:
Renders a ReflectionType (named, union, or intersection) as a string.
  Returns nil when the reflection type itself is nil (no declaration).

name: apropos
doc:
Returns a vector of symbols whose name contains the given search string.
  Searches across all loaded namespaces.

name: build-namespace-context
doc:
Builds a summary of available functions in the current namespace
  and its aliases for AI context.

name: build-symbol-context
doc: Builds AI context for a specific symbol: source code, docs, and metadata.

name: compile-str
doc: Compiles a Phel expression string to PHP code.

name: create-ns
doc:
Creates the given namespace if it does not already exist. Returns the
  namespace name in display form. Existing namespaces are left untouched.

name: dir
doc:
Prints all public definitions in the given namespace symbol or string.

  Returns nil. Prints one name per line, sorted alphabetically.

name: dir-fn
doc:
Prints all public definitions in the given namespace symbol or string.

  Returns nil. Prints one name per line, sorted alphabetically.

name: doc
doc: Prints the documentation for the given symbol.

name: embed-ns
doc:
Builds a searchable index of all public functions in a namespace.

  Each entry contains the function name, docstring, and embedding
  of the combined name+doc text. Useful for semantic code search.

  Options are passed through to `ai/embed`.

name: eval-capturing
doc:
Evaluates a string of Phel code while capturing stdout. Returns a hash-map
  with :value (the result), :out (captured stdout), :success (boolean), and
  :error (error message or nil).

  Useful for nREPL and other tooling that needs to separate printed output from
  return values.

name: eval-str
doc:
Evaluates a string of Phel code and returns the result.
  If the string contains multiple expressions, returns the result of the last one.

name: explain
doc:
Sends a Phel code string to the AI for explanation.

  Includes compilation output and namespace context to provide
  a thorough, grounded explanation.

name: explain-sym
doc: Explains a symbol by sending its source code and documentation to the AI.

name: find-fn
doc:
Searches for functions whose name or docstring contains the search string.
  Returns a vector of maps with :ns, :name, :doc, :private, :min-arity, :max-arity, :is-variadic.

name: find-ns
doc:
Returns the namespace name in display form if it is loaded, or nil if no
  namespace of that name exists. Accepts dot or backslash separators on input.

name: fix
doc:
Given Phel code that produced an error, sends both to the AI
  along with namespace context to suggest a fix.

name: get-source-code
doc:
Returns the source code of the definition identified by namespace and name
  strings, or nil if the source file cannot be found or metadata is missing.

name: get-src-dirs
doc:
Returns source directories for namespace resolution. Falls back to
  CommandFacade when src-dirs has not been initialized (e.g. outside vanilla REPL).

name: get-symbol-info
doc:
Returns a hash-map of structured metadata for the definition identified by
  namespace and name strings. Returns nil if no such definition exists.

  Keys: :doc, :file, :line, :column, :end-line, :end-column, :private,
        :deprecated, :min-arity, :max-arity, :is-variadic, :ns, :name

name: intern
doc:
Finds or creates a definition named by name-str in namespace ns-str,
  setting its root value to val when supplied (defaults to nil). The
  namespace is auto-registered by the underlying `addDefinition` call.
  Returns the fully qualified symbol (with the namespace in display form).

name: load-file
doc:
Loads and evaluates a Phel source file in the current REPL session.
  Reads the file content and evaluates it using the compiler, preserving
  the current REPL namespace context. Returns the result of the last expression.

name: loaded-namespaces
doc:
Returns all namespaces currently loaded in the REPL, in dot-separated
  display form.

name: macroexpand
doc:
Recursively expands the given form until it is no longer a macro call.
  The form must be quoted to prevent evaluation, matching Clojure semantics.

name: macroexpand-1
doc:
Expands the given form once if it is a macro call. The form must be
  quoted to prevent evaluation, matching Clojure semantics.

name: macroexpand-1-form
doc:
Expands the given form once if it is a macro call.
  Takes a quoted form and returns the expanded form, or the original
  form unchanged if it is not a macro call. Uses the CompilerFacade
  to perform the expansion without going through analyze+emit.

name: macroexpand-form
doc:
Recursively expands the given form until it is no longer a macro call.
  Takes a quoted form and returns the fully expanded form. Uses the
  CompilerFacade to perform the expansion without going through analyze+emit.

name: munge-ns
doc: Encodes a namespace string for registry lookup.

name: normalize-ns-str
doc: Converts backslashes to dots and remaps clojure.* to phel.* when the target exists.

name: normalize-require-symbol
doc: Normalizes a require symbol, returning the original if unchanged.

name: ns-aliases
doc:
Returns a hash-map of {alias => namespace} for all require aliases in the
  given namespace string. Target namespaces are returned in display form.

name: ns-interns
doc:
Returns a hash-map of {name => value} for every definition in the
  given namespace, including private ones. Returns an empty map if the
  namespace has no definitions.

name: ns-list
doc: Returns a sorted vector of all loaded namespace names in display form.

name: ns-publics
doc:
Returns a hash-map of {name => value} for all public definitions in the
  given namespace string. Private definitions are excluded.

name: ns-refers
doc:
Returns a hash-map of {name => source-namespace} for all referred symbols
  in the given namespace string. Source namespaces are returned in display form.

name: print-colorful
doc: Prints arguments with colored output.

name: print-colorful-str
doc: Same as print-str from core, but with color.

name: println-colorful
doc: Prints arguments with colored output followed by a newline.

name: remove-ns
doc:
Removes the namespace and all of its definitions from the registry.
  Use with caution. Returns nil.

name: require
doc:
Requires a Phel module into the environment.
  Accepts both the flat form and the Clojure-compatible vector form:
    (require 'phel\string :as str)
    (require '[phel\string :as str])
    (require '[phel\string :as str :refer [blank?]])

name: review
doc:
Sends Phel code to the AI for a code review, including namespace
  context for awareness of available functions and conventions.

name: search-doc
doc:
Searches docstrings across all loaded namespaces for the given string.
  Prints matching function names and their documentation.

name: search-ns
doc:
Semantic search over a namespace index built by `embed-ns`.

  Returns the k most relevant functions for the query.

name: source
doc: Returns the source code of the given symbol as a string, or nil if unavailable.

name: suggest
doc:
Describes what you want to accomplish in natural language and
  receives Phel code suggestions grounded in available functions.

name: symbol-info
doc:
Returns a hash-map of structured metadata for the given symbol, or nil if
  the symbol cannot be resolved.

  Keys: :doc, :file, :line, :column, :end-line, :end-column, :private,
        :deprecated, :min-arity, :max-arity, :is-variadic, :ns, :name

name: test-ns
doc:
Runs all tests in a given namespace from the REPL.
  Requires the namespace if not already loaded, finds all deftest definitions,
  runs them, prints results, and returns a hash-map with :pass, :fail, and :error counts.
  Preserves outer test state so it can be safely called during a test run.

name: use
doc: Adds a use statement to the environment.

name: compile-dispatch
doc: Builds a `{route-name → method-dispatch-map}` lookup for all routes.

name: compile-route-dispatch
doc:
For a single `[path data]` route and the global middleware, returns a map
   `{method-kw → [compiled-handler merged-data]}` with an optional `:default`
   entry for the method-agnostic top-level `:handler`.

name: compiled-router
doc:
Like `router` but performs Symfony's route compilation at macro-expansion
  time. The resulting router uses Symfony's `CompiledUrlMatcher`/`Generator`
  which are ~3x faster than their dynamic counterparts for large route
  tables.

  Because compilation runs during macro expansion, `raw-routes` must be a
  literal vector at the call site — it cannot be built from runtime values.
  Use `router` if your routes are dynamic.

name: dispatch-lookup
doc: Returns `[handler data]` for a given route-name and method, or nil.

name: extract-path-params
doc: Builds a Phel hash-map of path parameters, excluding Symfony's `_route` key.

name: flatten-routes
doc:
Flattens nested routes to a vector of `[path data]` tuples.

  Parent paths are concatenated with their children's paths and parent data
  maps are deep-merged into their children's data. `path-prefix` and
  `common-data` are merged into every route and let you mount a subtree under
  a prefix or share data across all routes.

name: generate-with
doc: Generates a URL using the given Symfony generator.

name: handler
doc:
Builds a `request -> response` function from a router.

  Matching flow per request:

  1. Resolve the request's path via `match-by-path`.
  2. Look up the handler for the request method in the precompiled dispatch
     table, falling back to the route's method-agnostic `:handler`.
  3. Invoke the handler with the request enriched with `[:attributes :match]`
     and `[:attributes :route-data]`. A `nil` response triggers the
     `:not-acceptable` handler.

  Options:

  | key                   | description |
  | ----------------------|-------------|
  | `:middleware`         | global middleware applied to every matched route
  | `:default-handler`    | fallback used for any 404/405/406 case not covered by a specific override
  | `:not-found`          | handler invoked when no route matches (HTTP 404)
  | `:method-not-allowed` | handler invoked when the path matches but no handler exists for the request method (HTTP 405)
  | `:not-acceptable`     | handler invoked when a matched handler returns `nil` (HTTP 406)

  Dispatch is precompiled at handler construction time, so per-request work
  is reduced to two hash-map lookups.

name: indexed-route->match
doc:
Converts an `[path data]` tuple from the compiled router's index into a
   by-name match response. Returns nil when the tuple is nil.

name: match-with
doc:
Runs the given Symfony matcher for `path` and builds a match result using
   `lookup-fn` to resolve `[template data]` for the matched route name.
   Returns nil when no route matches.

name: params->php-array
doc: Converts a Phel map of parameters into a PHP associative array keyed by name.

name: route-name-of
doc:
Returns the Symfony route name for a `[path data]` tuple, falling back to
   the path when `:name` isn't provided.

name: router
doc:
Builds a dynamic `Router` from a nested route tree.

  Routes are described as `[path data children*]` where `data` is an optional
  hash-map. Children inherit their parent's path prefix and have parent data
  deep-merged into their own. `data` may contain:

  - `:handler` — a 1-arg `request -> response` function (matches any method)
  - `:middleware` — a vector of `(fn [handler request])` wrappers
  - `:name` — a keyword used for URL generation via `match-by-name` / `generate`
  - method keys (`:get`, `:post`, …) — nested maps with their own `:handler`
    and `:middleware` that apply only for that HTTP method

  `options` accepts `:path` (prefix prepended to every route) and `:data`
  (merged into every route's data).

name: coerce
doc:
Walks `schema` and returns `value` with string-typed inputs coerced
  into their schema-required types. Already-typed values pass through.
  Unknown or untranslatable values are returned unchanged so validation
  can report the real failure.

name: conform
doc:
Coerces `value` against `schema`. Returns the coerced value if it
  then validates, otherwise the invalid marker `:phel.schema/invalid`.

name: explain
doc:
Returns `nil` if `value` conforms to `schema`, otherwise a map
  describing the violations.

name: human-readable-explain
doc:
Renders an explain result as a multi-line human string suitable for
  REPL or CI output. Returns `nil` for a `nil` result.

name: generate
doc:
Generates one random value conforming to `schema`. Accepts the same
  `:size` and `:seed` options as `phel\test\gen/generate`.

name: schema->gen
doc:
Returns a `phel\test\gen` generator for `schema`. Honours a
  `{:gen <gen>}` override in the schema options when present.

name: clear-instrumented!
doc: Removes every instrumentation entry. Returns `nil`.

name: function-schema?
doc:
Returns `true` if `schema` is a function schema of the shape
  `[:=> args-schema return-schema]`.

name: instrument!
doc:
Registers `f` under `name` (any key) wrapped with `schema`. Returns
  the wrapped fn. Subsequent calls to `unstrument!` with the same name
  can restore the original via `(instrumented-original name)`.

name: instrumented-original
doc:
Returns the original, unwrapped function associated with `name`, or
  `nil` if no instrumentation is registered under `name`.

name: instrumented?
doc: Returns `true` if `name` currently has an instrumentation entry.

name: schema-check?
doc: Returns `true` when runtime validation is enabled.

name: schema?
doc:
Returns `true` if `x` has the shape of a schema value (a keyword or a
  vector whose head is a keyword, including the `:=>` function marker).

name: set-schema-check!
doc:
Enables (`true`) or disables (`false`) runtime validation performed by
  `wrap-with-schema`/`instrument!`. Returns the new value.

name: unstrument!
doc:
Unregisters the instrumentation bound to `name` and returns the
  original (unwrapped) function if present, otherwise `nil`.

name: with-schema-check
doc:
Runs thunk `f` with runtime validation set to `enabled?`, restoring
  the previous value even if `f` throws.

name: wrap-with-function-schema
doc:
Convenience: accepts a `[:=> args-schema return-schema]` schema vector
  and returns `f` wrapped accordingly.

name: wrap-with-schema
doc:
Wraps `f` so each call validates its arguments against `arg-schema`
  (a vector of per-arg schemas) and its return value against
  `return-schema`. When `schema-check?` returns `false` at call time
  the wrapper short-circuits and invokes `f` directly, skipping
  validation on both sides.

name: clear!
doc: Removes every user-registered schema. Returns `nil`.

name: deref-ref
doc:
Returns the schema registered under `name`, or `nil` if no schema is
  registered with that name.

name: register!
doc:
Registers `schema` under `name` (usually a keyword). Overwrites any
  previous entry. Returns the registered schema.

name: registered?
doc: Returns `true` if a schema is registered under `name`.

name: registry-snapshot
doc:
Returns the current registry as a plain map. Intended for inspection
  and testing.

name: unregister!
doc: Removes the schema bound to `name`. Returns `nil`.

name: extract-options
doc:
Returns `[options remaining]` where `options` is a map (possibly
  empty) of trailing options pulled from the second position of a
  parametric schema, and `remaining` is the rest of the args after
  the options map.

name: map-entry-optional?
doc:
Returns `true` when a `[:map ...]` entry is declared with
  `{:optional true}`.

name: map-entry-options
doc:
Options map for a `[:map ...]` entry `[key opts? schema]`. Returns an
  empty map when the entry has no options position.

name: map-entry-schema
doc:
Inner schema of a `[:map ...]` entry, skipping the options map when
  present.

name: pattern-source
doc:
Returns the raw regex string for a `:re` schema. Accepts either a
  string pattern (used verbatim) or a compiled PHP regex handle.

name: resolve-or-default
doc:
Like `resolve-or-throw`, but returns `default` when `head` is not
  registered instead of throwing. Used by `coerce` where unknown heads
  are intentionally passed through unchanged for downstream validation
  to flag.

name: resolve-or-throw
doc:
Resolves an unknown head by looking it up in the registry. When
  `head` names a registered schema, invokes `f` with the registered
  schema; otherwise throws an `InvalidArgumentException` mentioning
  `label` (e.g. `"unknown schema kind"` or `"no generator for schema kind"`).

  Every head-dispatching caller uses this so the error shape is
  consistent across validator/explainer/coercer/generator.

name: schema-args
doc:
Returns the positional arguments of `schema` (children past the
  head and optional options map).

name: schema-head
doc:
Returns the head (kind keyword) of `schema`. Keyword schemas are
  their own head; vector schemas use their first element.

name: schema-options
doc: Returns the options map of `schema` or `{}` if none.

name: valid-inst?
doc:
PHP has no native instant type; canonical inst values are
  `\DateTimeInterface` instances.

name: valid-seqable?
doc: Collections that `seq` accepts.

name: valid-sequential?
doc: Vectors and lists are sequential.

name: valid?
doc: Returns `true` if `value` conforms to `schema`, otherwise `false`.

name: validate-collection
doc: Generic collection validator used by `[:vector s]` and `[:set s]`.

name: coerce
doc:
Walks `schema` and coerces string-shaped input into schema-required
  types. Idempotent for already-typed values.

name: conform
doc:
Coerces `value` against `schema`. Returns the coerced value on
  success, otherwise `:phel.schema/invalid`.

name: deref-ref
doc: Returns the schema registered under `name`, or `nil`.

name: explain
doc:
Returns `nil` when `value` conforms to `schema`. On mismatch returns
  `{:schema schema :value value :errors [...]}` with one error per
  violation, each carrying `:path`, `:in`, `:schema`, `:value`, `:type`.

name: generate
doc:
Generates a single value conforming to `schema`. Accepts `:size` and
  `:seed` options.

name: human-readable-explain
doc:
Renders an `explain` result as a multi-line human string. Returns
  `nil` for a `nil` input.

name: instrument!
doc:
Registers `f` wrapped with `schema` under `name`. Returns the wrapped
  function. The original is preserved so `unstrument!` can restore it.

name: instrumented?
doc: Returns `true` if `name` is currently instrumented.

name: invalid-marker
doc:
Sentinel returned by `conform` when a value cannot be made to fit a
  schema.

name: register!
doc: Registers `schema` under `name` in the global schema registry.

name: registered?
doc: Returns `true` if a schema is registered under `name`.

name: schema->gen
doc: Returns the `phel\test\gen` generator associated with `schema`.

name: schema-args
doc:
Returns the positional arguments of `schema` (children past the head
  and optional options map).

name: schema-check?
doc:
Returns `true` when runtime validation performed by the instrument
  helpers is currently enabled.

name: schema-head
doc: Returns the dispatch head (kind keyword) of `schema`.

name: schema-options
doc: Returns the options map of `schema` or `{}`.

name: schema?
doc: Returns `true` if `x` has the shape of a schema value.

name: set-schema-check!
doc:
Enables (`true`) or disables (`false`) runtime validation. Returns
  the new value.

name: unregister!
doc: Removes the schema bound to `name`. Returns `nil`.

name: unstrument!
doc:
Removes the instrumentation registered under `name` and returns the
  original, unwrapped function (or `nil` if no entry).

name: validate
doc: Returns `true` if `value` conforms to `schema`, otherwise `false`.

name: with-schema-check
doc:
Invokes zero-arg thunk `f` with runtime validation forced to
  `enabled?`. The previous value is restored on return or exception.

name: wrap-with-function-schema
doc: Wraps `f` with the `[:=> args ret]` function schema.

name: wrap-with-schema
doc:
Wraps `f` so calls validate arguments and return values against the
  supplied schemas.

name: as-pattern
doc:
Ensures match is a regex pattern. If it looks like a delimited regex
  (first and last chars match), returns as-is; otherwise wraps as literal.

name: blank?
doc:
True if s is nil, empty, or contains only whitespace. Non-breaking
  separators (`U+00A0`, `U+2007`, `U+202F`) are not treated as whitespace.

name: capitalize
doc: Converts first character to upper-case and all other characters to lower-case.

name: chars
doc:
Returns a vector of characters from string s.

  This is a convenience function for converting strings to character sequences.
  Properly handles multibyte UTF-8 characters.

name: contains?
doc: True if s contains substr.

name: ends-with?
doc: True if s ends with substr.

name: escape
doc: Returns a new string with each character escaped according to cmap.

name: includes?
doc: True if s includes substr.

name: index-of
doc: Returns the index of value in s, or nil if not found.

name: join
doc: Returns a string of all elements in coll, separated by an optional separator.

name: last-index-of
doc: Returns the last index of value in s, or nil if not found.

name: lower-case
doc: Converts string to all lower-case.

name: pad-both
doc: Returns a string padded on both sides to length len.

name: pad-left
doc: Returns a string padded on the left side to length len.

name: pad-right
doc: Returns a string padded on the right side to length len.

name: re-quote-replacement
doc: Escapes special characters in a replacement string for literal use.

name: repeat
doc: Returns a string containing n copies of s.

name: replace
doc: Replaces all instances of match with replacement in s.

name: replace-first
doc: Replaces the first instance of match with replacement in s.

name: reverse
doc: Returns s with its characters reversed.

name: split
doc: Splits string on a regular expression, returning a vector of parts.

name: split-lines
doc: Splits s on \n or \r\n. Trailing empty lines are not returned.

name: starts-with?
doc: True if s starts with substr.

name: subs
doc: Returns the substring of s from start (inclusive) to end (exclusive).

name: trim
doc: Removes whitespace from both ends of string.

name: trim-newline
doc: Removes all trailing newline or return characters from string.

name: triml
doc: Removes whitespace from the left side of string.

name: trimr
doc: Removes whitespace from the right side of string.

name: upper-case
doc: Converts string to all upper-case.

name: boolean
doc: Generator of booleans.

name: char
doc: Generator of printable ASCII characters (space through `~`).

name: char-alpha
doc: Generator of ASCII letters.

name: char-alphanumeric
doc: Generator of ASCII letters and digits.

name: choose
doc: Generator of integers in the closed interval `[lo hi]`.

name: default-num-tests
doc: Number of trials `quick-check` runs by default.

name: default-size
doc: Magnitude used when no `:size` option is supplied.

name: defspec
doc:
Defines a property test. The generated `deftest` runs `quick-check`
  and asserts the result is `:pass`. `options` is a hash-map accepting
  `:num-tests`, `:size`, `:seed` and `:shrink?`.

  Attach `^:no-shrink` metadata to the name to skip shrinking on
  failure. The `test-name` symbol's metadata is also forwarded to the
  underlying `deftest`, so tag-based selectors apply as usual.

  On failure a `:defspec-failed` event is sent to the reporter set
  before the surrounding `is` assertion records a `:failed` event.
  Reporters that want rich shrink information can subscribe to it; the
  built-in reporters keep rendering their usual failure summary.

  Shape: `(defspec name options args-gen property)`.

name: elements
doc: Generator that picks a random element from `coll`.

name: emit-spec-failure-event!
doc:
Fans out a `:defspec-failed` event carrying the rich outcome map so
  reporters can surface the shrunk counterexample, seed, and shrink
  step count.

name: float
doc: Generator of floats in `[0, 1)`.

name: fmap
doc: Returns a generator that applies `f` to values produced by `g`.

name: frequency
doc:
Generator that picks one of the `[weight gen]` pairs with probability
  proportional to weight.

name: generate
doc: Runs `g` once and returns a single value. Accepts `:size` and `:seed`.

name: int
doc: Generator of integers in `[-size, size]`.

name: keyword
doc: Generator of keywords with alphabetic names, length in `[1, max(1, size)]`.

name: large-int
doc: Generator of arbitrary PHP-range integers.

name: list-of
doc: Generator of lists whose elements come from `g`. Length in `[0, size]`.

name: map-of
doc:
Generator of hash-maps with keys from `kg` and values from `vg`. Number of
  entries is in `[0, size]`.

name: nat
doc: Generator of non-negative integers in `[0, size]`.

name: one-of
doc: Generator that selects uniformly from `gens` and runs the chosen one.

name: quick-check
doc:
Runs `property` for `num-tests` trials, drawing each trial's arguments from
  `args-gen` (a generator returning a vector of arguments). Returns a hash-map
  with `:result` (`:pass`, `:failed`, or `:error`), `:num-tests`, and the
  effective `:seed` for replay. On failure/error the failing `:args` (and
  `:exception`) are also included.

  Options:
  - `:size` (default 100): magnitude passed to the generator.
  - `:seed` (default: fresh per-run): PRNG seed.
  - `:shrink?` (default: true): when true, a failing trial is shrunk to
    a minimal counterexample; the resulting map carries `:shrunk-args`,
    `:original-args` and `:shrink-steps`.
example: (quick-check 50 (tuple int int) (fn [a b] (= (+ a b) (+ b a))))
arities: (quick-check num-tests args-gen property {:size size :seed seed :shrink? shrink?})

name: resize
doc: Returns a generator equivalent to `g` but with `size` forced to `n`.

name: return
doc: Generator that always yields `x`.

name: sample
doc:
Runs `g` `num-samples` times (default 10) and returns a vector of values.
  Accepts `:size` and `:seed`.

name: set-of
doc: Generator of hash-sets with elements from `g`. Cardinality in `[0, size]`.

name: shrink-outcome
doc:
Given a failing trial `outcome`, runs the shrink driver on its args
  and returns an outcome augmented with `:original-args`, `:shrunk-args`
  and `:shrink-steps`. If `shrink?` is falsy, returns `outcome`
  unchanged.

name: sized
doc:
Builds a generator from a function `f` of `size`. The returned generator
  forwards its `size` into `f`, which must yield another generator that is
  then invoked with the same size.

name: spec-failure-message
doc:
Renders the human-readable failure message for a `defspec` outcome
  map. Includes the shrink summary when the trial's arguments were
  shrunk to a smaller counterexample.

name: string
doc: Generator of printable ASCII strings, length in `[0, size]`.

name: string-alpha
doc: Generator of ASCII alphabetic strings, length in `[0, size]`.

name: string-alphanumeric
doc: Generator of ASCII alphanumeric strings, length in `[0, size]`.

name: such-that
doc:
Generator yielding only values from `g` that satisfy `pred`. Retries up to
  `max-tries` (default 100) before throwing.

name: symbol
doc: Generator of symbols with alphabetic names, length in `[1, max(1, size)]`.

name: tuple
doc:
Generator of a fixed-length vector produced by running each of the given
  generators in order. Accepts either a vector of generators or variadic
  generator arguments.

name: vector-of
doc:
Generator of vectors. Length is `[0, size]` with one arg, exactly `n` with
  `(vector-of g n)`, or `[lo, hi]` with `(vector-of g lo hi)`.

name: int-rose-tree
doc: Rose tree for an integer `n` that shrinks toward zero.

name: int-rose-tree-towards
doc: Rose tree for `n` whose children shrink strictly toward `target`.

name: lazy-concat
doc: One-element-at-a-time concatenation of two lazy seqs.

name: lazy-filter
doc: One-element-at-a-time `filter`.

name: lazy-map
doc:
Element-wise `(map f coll)` that realises one element at a time.
  Necessary because the built-in `map` realises a full chunk at once,
  which is incompatible with the self-recursive rose-tree structure.

name: positional-shrinks
doc:
For index `i`, emits a lazy seq of variants of `trees` where only
  position `i` has been replaced with each of its shrinks.

name: rose-bind
doc:
Monadic bind. `f` takes a value and returns a rose tree; the resulting
  tree combines the shrinks of `t` (each fed through `f`) with the
  shrinks produced by `f` on the root.

name: rose-children
doc: Returns the lazy sequence of immediate child rose trees.

name: rose-filter
doc:
Returns the subtree consisting only of nodes whose value satisfies
  `pred`. Children that fail `pred` are pruned. If the root fails
  `pred`, returns `nil` (caller is responsible for handling).

name: rose-fmap
doc:
Applies `f` to every value in rose tree `t` (the root and, lazily,
  every descendant).

name: rose-join
doc: Flattens a rose tree of rose trees into a single rose tree.

name: rose-map
doc:
Rose tree for a hash-map. `entry-trees` is a vector of rose trees of
  `[k v]` pairs. Shrinks by removing entries and by shrinking each
  pair in place.

name: rose-pure
doc: Leaf rose tree: value `x` with no shrink candidates.

name: rose-root
doc: Returns the root value of rose tree `t`.

name: rose-shrinks
doc:
Alias for `rose-children`: the lazy sequence of immediate smaller
  variants of the current root.

name: rose-string
doc: Rose tree for a string whose elements are char rose trees.

name: rose-tree
doc:
Rose tree constructor. `children` should be a lazy sequence of rose
  trees (or any seqable value).

name: rose-vector
doc:
Rose tree for a vector whose children are built from the rose trees
  of its elements. Shrinks by removing elements and by shrinking each
  element in place.

name: rose-vector-lax
doc:
Like `rose-vector` but preserves original length; only shrinks each
  element in place (no removal).

name: rose-zip
doc:
Takes a vector of rose trees and returns a rose tree whose root is
  the vector of roots and whose children shrink one position at a time.

name: rose?
doc: Returns `true` if `x` looks like a rose tree.

name: shrink-int
doc:
Shrink strategy toward zero: halving steps (`n/2`, `n/4`, …) and then
  decrement toward zero.

name: shrink-int-towards
doc:
Returns a seq of integer candidates strictly closer to `target` than
  `n`. Yields the target first, then halving steps.

name: shrink-vector-by-removal
doc:
Candidates formed by dropping a leading block of halving sizes, then
  single-element drops.

name: shrinks-of-many
doc:
Given a vector of rose trees, returns a lazy sequence of rose-tree
  vectors where each vector shrinks exactly one of the inputs in turn.

name: shrinks-of-many*
doc: Helper: lazily iterates each position in turn.

name: compile-filter-regex
doc:
Wraps a user-supplied regex body in PCRE delimiters when it is not
  already a `/.../` pattern. Treats bare fragments as substring
  matchers.

name: glob->regex
doc:
Converts a namespace glob (`phel.http.*`) into an anchored PCRE
  pattern. `.` is treated literally, `*` matches any run of non-`.`
  characters, `**` matches anything. The glob is case-sensitive.

name: has-selectors?
doc:
Returns `true` when `options` contains at least one non-empty
  selector key.

name: has-tag?
doc:
Returns `true` when `meta` carries `tag` (a keyword or a string
  treated as a keyword). Single-keyword metadata (`^:integration`) and
  map-based multi-tag metadata (`^{:tags [:integration :slow]}`) both
  match.

name: keep-test?
doc:
Returns `true` when the test described by `meta` and `ns-name`
  should be run under `options`. `options` is a map that may carry any
  of `:include`, `:exclude`, `:ns-patterns`, `:filters`. Selectors that
  are absent or empty impose no restriction; specified selectors are
  AND'd together.

name: matches-exclude?
doc:
Returns `true` when any tag in `excludes` is truthy on `meta`. An
  empty or nil `excludes` vector always returns `false` (nothing
  excluded).

name: matches-filter?
doc:
Returns `true` when `patterns` is empty (no restriction) or when any
  entry in `patterns` matches `test-name`.

name: matches-include?
doc:
Returns `true` when `includes` is empty (no restriction) or when any
  tag in `includes` is truthy on `meta`.

name: matches-ns?
doc:
Returns `true` when `patterns` is empty (no restriction) or when any
  glob in `patterns` matches `ns-name`.

name: name-matches?
doc:
Returns `true` when `pattern` (a PCRE `/.../` string or a plain
  substring) matches `test-name`.

name: non-empty-vec?
doc:
Returns `true` when `xs` is a non-nil, non-empty vector/seq. Used to
  check whether a selector option was supplied by the caller.

name: normalize-ns
doc:
Normalizes a namespace name so both `phel\test\foo` and
  `phel.test.foo` are interchangeable for glob matching.

name: ns-matches?
doc:
Returns `true` when `ns-name` matches the glob `pattern`. Supports
  `*` (single segment) and `**` (any run). Backslash-separated
  namespaces (`phel\http\client`) are treated as dotted
  (`phel.http.client`) so globs stay portable.

name: tag-key
doc:
Coerces a selector tag (keyword or string) into the keyword form used
  to look up metadata. Returns `nil` for other inputs.

name: truthy-tag?
doc:
True when `meta` contains a truthy value at `kw`. Also accepts
  vector-valued `:tags` metadata, checking membership by keyword.

name: args->rose
doc:
Rose tree whose root is `args` and children shrink each positional
  argument in place using its value-based shrinker. Arguments are
  never dropped (they are function parameters, not collection
  elements).

name: fails?
doc:
Returns `true` when `pred` fails for `value` (either returning a
  non-truthy result or throwing).

name: shrink
doc:
Walks rose tree `tree` depth-first, greedily descending into any
  child whose root still fails `pred`. Returns
  `{:smallest v :shrink-steps n :tree final-tree}`.

name: shrink-args
doc:
Shrinks a failing args vector using `property`. Returns
  `{:smallest args :shrink-steps n}` where `args` is the smallest args
  vector that still makes `property` fail.

name: value->rose
doc:
Builds a rose tree for `v` using the built-in shrink strategy that
  matches its runtime type. Integers shrink toward zero; strings,
  vectors, lists, hash-maps and sets shrink by element removal plus
  recursive element shrinks; everything else is a leaf.

name: *testing-contexts*
doc: Stack of testing context strings, most recent first.

name: add-reporter!
doc:
Appends `reporter-fn` to the active reporter set. Returns the updated
  reporter list.

name: announce-seed!
doc:
Prints `Seed: <n>` once at the start of a randomized run so failures
  can be reproduced with `--seed=<n>`.

name: are
doc:
Checks multiple assertions with a template expression.
  `argv` is a vector of template variables, `expr` is the assertion template,
  and the remaining `args` are partitioned by `(count argv)` to fill the template.
  Template variables are substituted lexically at macro-expansion time, so
  literal collection cells (e.g. `()`, `[]`, `{}`) are preserved as data and
  are not evaluated as code.

name: bump-junit-counters
doc:
Increments `:tests`, plus `:failures`/`:errors` based on the event's
  `:state`. Used to aggregate both the per-suite and per-run totals.

name: clear-reporters!
doc: Removes every registered reporter. Returns an empty vector.

name: coerce-reporter
doc:
Turns a single `:reporters` entry (function, keyword, or string) into
  a reporter function. Throws on unknown names or invalid values.

name: collection-diff-applicable?
doc:
Returns true when a `=`/`not=` failure carries two same-shape
  collections big enough to benefit from a stacked diff.

name: compose-two-fixtures
doc: Returns a fixture that applies f1 around a fixture that applies f2 around g.

name: decorate-event
doc:
Prepends testing-context information to the event message and injects
  the current test name.

name: default-fixture
doc: Identity fixture: just invokes the wrapped function.

name: default-reporter
doc:
Human-readable dot output. Preserves the legacy behavior: `.` for
  pass, `F` for fail, `E` for error, plus periodic newlines so long
  runs wrap at 80 columns. `S` marks a skipped test.

name: deftest
doc:
Defines a test function.

  Metadata attached to `test-name` is forwarded to the defined function
  so selectors can inspect it at runtime. `^:integration` (shorthand
  for `{:integration true}`) and `^{:tags [:integration :slow]}`
  multi-tag maps are both honoured.

name: diff-worth-rendering?
doc:
Decides whether `expected` and `actual` are large enough to justify a
  block-style diff. Below the thresholds the existing summary line is
  more readable than the diff.

name: do-report
doc:
Add file and line information to a test result and call report.
  If you are writing a custom assert-expr method, call this function
  to pass test results to report.

name: dot-reporter
doc:
Minimal CI-friendly reporter. Prints `.` per pass, `F` per failure,
  `E` per error, `S` per skipped test, and a compact one-line summary
  at the end. Does not print failure/error diagnostics.

name: emit-marker!
doc: Prints a single progress marker and wraps the line every 80 markers.

name: find-test-vars
doc:
Discovers every `deftest`-defined function in `ns` and returns a
  vector of `{:fn <callable> :meta <map>}` entries. The caller is
  responsible for applying selectors.

name: generate-seed
doc: Returns a fresh non-negative integer seed suitable for PHP's RNG.

name: get-failed-tests
doc:
Returns the names (`ns/test-name`) of tests that failed or errored
  in the last run. Used by `--parallel` orchestration to aggregate
  last-failed lists across worker processes.

name: get-reporters
doc: Returns the currently registered reporter functions as a vector.

name: get-stats
doc: Returns the current test statistics as a hash-map with :failed and :counts keys.

name: is
doc: Asserts that an expression is true.

name: join-fixtures
doc: Composes a collection of fixtures into a single fixture function.

name: junit-ensure-current
doc:
Ensures `state` has a `:current` suite; lazily initialised from the
  event's `:ns` when a testcase arrives outside a `begin-test-ns`.

name: junit-reporter
doc:
JUnit-XML v1 output. Emits a `<testsuites>` root with one
  `<testsuite>` per Phel namespace. Each assertion becomes a
  `<testcase>`; failures and errors are nested accordingly.

name: legacy-filter-matches?
doc:
Back-compat: the original `--filter` option accepted a single
  substring matched against the test name. When selectors are also
  active, this check still applies so existing callers keep behaving.

name: maybe-shuffle-tests
doc:
Returns `tests` shuffled when `:random-order` is set in `options` (or
  an explicit `:seed` is supplied), or unchanged otherwise. The active
  seed (`:seed-resolved`) reseeds PHP's Mersenne Twister so the resulting
  order is reproducible.

name: only-tests-matches?
doc:
Returns true when `only-tests` is empty (no restriction) or when
  `ns/test-name` matches one of the entries verbatim.

name: partition-tests
doc:
Splits the discovered tests into a `{:keep [...] :skip [...]}` map
  using the selector options. `:keep` preserves original order; each
  `:skip` entry is annotated with its metadata so reporters can surface
  skip events.

name: print-collection-diff
doc:
Prints a unified-diff-like block comparing the `expected` and `actual`
  collections. Maps show added/removed/changed keys with `+`, `-`, `~`;
  vectors and lists show index-aligned `+`, `-`, ` ` rows; sets show the
  symmetric difference. Callers should invoke this only after checking
  `same-shape?` and `diff-worth-rendering?`.

name: print-form-evaluated
doc:
Prints the `Form: ... / evaluated to: ...` pair shared by every
  failure printer that reports a single value and its computed result.

name: print-label
doc:
Prints `label:`, the readable form of `value`, then any extra
  trailing words on a single line. Used by the built-in failure
  printers to keep the right-aligned two-column layout consistent.

name: print-summary
doc:
Emits the `:summary` event to the active reporter set.
  Kept for backwards compatibility; prefer letting `run-tests` emit the
  event at the end of the run.

name: quote-if-empty-list
doc:
Wraps an empty-list cell in `(quote ())` so it survives compilation as
  literal data. Phel's evaluator cannot apply an empty list as a call, so a
  bare `()` placed in value position (e.g. as an `are` template cell) must be
  quoted for the generated code to compile. Non-empty lists and other values
  are returned unchanged — the caller can quote explicitly if needed.

name: record-stats!
doc: Mutates the internal stats atom based on an assertion-result event.

name: register-reporter!
doc:
Registers a custom reporter function under `name` (keyword or
  keyword-castable string). Returns `name`.

name: repeat-count
doc: Returns the validated `:repeat` count from `options`, defaulting to 1.

name: requested-reporters
doc:
Returns the user-selected reporter identifiers, honouring the
  `--testdox` shortcut and defaulting to `[:default]`.

name: reset-stats
doc:
Resets the test statistics to their initial state.
  Call this before running a new batch of tests to get fresh results.

name: resolve-reporter
doc:
Returns the reporter function registered for `name` (keyword or
  string). Checks user-registered reporters before the built-in set.
  Returns `nil` if the name is unknown.

name: resolve-reporters-option
doc:
Resolves the `:reporters` option into a vector of reporter functions.
  Accepts a sequence of keywords or strings (built-in names), or a
  sequence of functions, or a mix. Defaults to `[:default]`.

name: resolve-seed
doc:
Returns the seed `run-tests` should use, or `nil` when ordering is
  deterministic and no seed was requested. An explicit `:seed` always
  wins; `:random-order` without a seed gets a freshly generated one.

name: restore-stats
doc: Restores test statistics from a previously saved state.

name: run-tests
doc:
Runs all tests in the given namespaces. When `:list-only` is true,
  prints the discovered tests and skips execution.

  Recognized option keys include `:filter`, `:filters`, `:include`,
  `:exclude`, `:ns-patterns`, `:fail-fast`, `:stack-trace`, `:reporters`,
  `:junit-output`, `:list-only`, `:only-tests`, `:last-failed-file`,
  `:slowest`, `:repeat` (run the selected tests N times), `:seed`
  (integer seed for the order RNG), and `:random-order` (shuffle tests
  per namespace).

name: same-shape?
doc:
Returns true when `a` and `b` are both maps, both sets, or both
  sequential. Mixed-shape pairs fall back to the summary printer.

name: selector-options
doc:
Extracts the tag/namespace selector subset from the full options map.
  Name-based filters (`:filter` / `:filters`) are handled separately as
  discovery filters and are intentionally excluded here.

name: sequential?
doc:
Returns true when `v` is a vector or a list: the two ordered shapes
  the diff renderer aligns by index.

name: set-junit-output!
doc:
Configures the output path the JUnit reporter writes to. When `nil`,
  the XML is printed to stdout.

name: set-reporters!
doc:
Replaces the active reporter set with `reporters` (a sequence of
  single-argument functions). Returns the new reporter list.

name: skip-reason
doc:
Returns `:selector` when the test is excluded by a tag or namespace
  selector, or `nil` when it should run. Name-based filters
  (`:filter` / `:filters`) are applied upstream as discovery filters and
  never reach this function.

name: sort-by-readable
doc:
Sorts `coll` by the readable representation of each entry. Used to
  give the diff a deterministic order even when keys or values mix
  types that Phel's default comparator rejects.

name: substitute-symbols
doc:
Recursively replaces every occurrence of a key in `smap` within `form` with
  its corresponding value, walking lists, vectors, hash-maps, and hash-sets.
  Used by `are` to expand template cells at macro-expansion time rather than
  let-binding them at runtime.

name: successful?
doc: Checks if all tests passed.

name: tap-reporter
doc:
TAP v13 output. Emits `TAP version 13`, `1..N` plan, `ok`/`not ok`
  lines per assertion, and a YAML block per failure. `N` is the total
  number of assertions observed during the run.

name: testdox-reporter
doc:
Per-assertion single-line description used by the `--reporter=testdox`
  flag.

name: testing
doc:
Adds a testing context string. Used inside deftest to describe a group of assertions.
  The context string is prepended to failure messages for better diagnostics.

name: use-fixtures
doc:
Registers fixture functions for the current namespace.

  `fixture-type` is either `:each` (wraps every individual test) or
  `:once` (wraps the whole run in a single function). Each fixture is
  a function of one argument — a thunk `(fn [])` representing the tests
  to run — and is expected to invoke that thunk somewhere in its body.

  Calling `use-fixtures` with no fixture functions removes all fixtures
  of that type previously registered on the namespace.

name: visible-test-pred
doc:
Returns the predicate that decides whether a discovered test passes
  the discovery filters (`:filter`, `:filters`, `:only-tests`).

name: visible-tests-for-ns
doc:
Returns the discovered tests in `ns` that survive the discovery filters
  (`:filter`, `:filters`, `:only-tests`). Tag and namespace selectors are
  applied later by `partition-tests` so they can surface as skip events.
  Honours `:random-order` to shuffle the result deterministically.

name: write-last-failed!
doc:
Persists the failed-test list to `path` so a subsequent
  `--last-failed` run can replay it. Always overwrites; an empty list
  produces an empty file.

name: decode
doc: Recursive Transit decoder over a `json_decode` result tree.

name: decode-array
doc:
Decodes a JSON array. Detects `["~#tag", rep]` markers before
  falling back to a positional vector decode.

name: decode-cmap
doc:
Decodes a `~#cmap` payload — a flat sequence of alternating key/value
  representations — into a persistent map.

name: decode-object
doc:
Decodes a JSON object (as PHP associative array) into a Phel map.
  String keys may themselves be Transit-encoded (e.g. `"~:foo"`).

name: decode-tagged-array
doc:
Decodes a `["~#tag", rep]` array. Handles built-in collection tags
  (`set`, `list`, `cmap`) and falls back to `:handlers` / `:default-handler`.

name: decode-tagged-scalar
doc:
Decodes a `~`-prefixed string. Returns the decoded value, or the
  original string when the prefix is one of the escape forms.

name: encode
doc:
Encodes a Phel value into the PHP-array shape consumed by
  `json_encode`. Strings carrying a Transit-sensitive prefix are
  escaped with a leading `~`.

name: escape-string
doc:
Escapes a plain Phel string so that an existing leading `~`, `^`, or
  `` ` `` is not mistaken for a Transit tag by the reader.

name: read-string
doc:
Reads one Transit+JSON-Verbose value from string `s`.

  Options:
    :handlers         map of tag-string to 1-arg fn for `~#tag` extensions
    :default-handler  2-arg fn `(fn [tag rep] ...)` invoked for any
                      unknown tag (both scalar and array forms). Receives
                      the bare tag name (e.g. "point", ":", "~") and
                      the already-decoded representation.

name: starts-with?
doc: True when `s` begins with the single character `c`.

name: string-keys?
doc: True when every key in `m` is a plain Phel string.

name: tag-string
doc:
Returns the tag portion of a `~#tag`-encoded array marker, or nil
  when `s` is not such a marker.

name: write-string
doc: Serialises `value` to a Transit+JSON-Verbose string.

name: keywordize-keys
doc: Recursively transforms all string keys in hash-maps to keywords.

name: postwalk
doc:
Performs a depth-first, post-order traversal of `form`. Calls `f` on each
  sub-form, uses `f`'s return value in place of the original. Walks into
  vectors, lists, hash-maps, and hash-sets.

name: postwalk-replace
doc:
Recursively transforms `form` by replacing every occurrence of a key in
  `smap` with the corresponding value. Applies replacements bottom-up.

name: prewalk
doc:
Like `postwalk`, but does a pre-order traversal (applies `f` before recursing
  into children).

name: prewalk-replace
doc:
Recursively transforms `form` by replacing every occurrence of a key in
  `smap` with the corresponding value. Applies replacements top-down.

name: stringify-keys
doc: Recursively transforms all keyword keys in hash-maps to strings.

name: walk
doc:
Traverses `form`, an arbitrary data structure. Applies `inner` to each
  element of `form`, building up a data structure of the same type, then
  applies `outer` to the result. Recognizes vectors, lists, hash-maps,
  and hash-sets. Other types are returned as-is.

name: clear-on-reload
doc: Removes every hook registered for `namespace`.

name: register-on-reload
doc:
Registers a zero-arg function to run every time `namespace` is
  reloaded by the watcher. Replaces any previously registered hook
  with the same `name`.

name: run-on-reload-hooks
doc:
Executes every hook registered for `namespace`. Returns the
  number of hooks that fired.

name: watch!
doc:
Starts the file watcher on the given vector of paths. Blocks until
  the watcher is stopped (e.g. Ctrl+C). Reloads changed namespaces in
  dependency order and runs any hooks registered with `register-on-reload`.
